headline: Korean robot maker Doosan Robotics says it has won state backing for two AI robot projects worth 98.9 billion won in total.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a sizeable state-backed robot and chip programme, but a research grant with products due only from 2031 and every target set by the company itself.
importance_line: Skilled welders and Korean manufacturers short of workers are the people most affected, since the robots are meant to learn and reproduce skilled workers' know-how, but the products are not due until 2031 and every target is Doosan Robotics' own.
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports that Doosan Robotics, a Korean maker of collaborative robots (robots built to work alongside people), said on 6 Oct 2026 that two of its proposals were selected as state-backed projects with a combined research budget of 98.9 billion won (about $70 million), of which 68.1 billion won is government money. One project would put a Korean-made AI chip inside three collaborative-robot models (an industrial humanoid is also planned) so they can see, decide and act on site without an outside computer or cloud, with sales planned from 2031; the other would teach robots to weld nuclear power plant parts by learning from skilled welders, with Doosan's own targets of matching their paths at 95% or better and cutting multilayer welding time by more than 50%.
notes: The Korea Herald page (the pool's original) was not reachable here (HTTP 000); the same Doosan Robotics announcement was read in Seoul Economic Daily (credited, its own reporting), Chosunbiz and Korea IT Times, which agree. The dollar figure is Korea IT Times'. A funding and plans story, with no robot shown at work yet, so machine_action is false.
